lines.text: Step five: run. Run greyed out? The reason is beside it, such as Pick a scan first.
With conditions in place and no red line, Run is ready.
Press Run. On a phone, it is in the bottom bar.
A long list shows a progress line; the button beside it ends the run early and keeps what was read.
If your broker's limit held some stocks back, a note says so. Run again in a minute to include them.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
The header reads Matched N of M: green above zero, amber at zero.
The time pill says when it ran.
The table lists matches first. Each row says Matched, Did not match, or Could not be read, with the reason.
Could not be read never counts as did not match.
Auto-refresh runs the same scan again every minute while the page is open. Export downloads the table as a spreadsheet file.
The stocks that did not match are counted here; one tap lists them.
Save matches as a watchlist keeps them under My watchlists.
Show on chart opens the chart in place, with only the scan's own conditions drawn.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
Where does the data come from? With your own broker: every timeframe, 1 minute to Monthly, within its limits.
Without a broker: Daily, Weekly and Monthly from ATP's stored end-of-day history. For 1 minute to 1 hour, connect your broker.
A stock not stored yet is read through your own broker; without one, its row says so.
There is no shared live data: live data comes only from your own broker.
After a run, hover over the time pill: it names the source, your broker or ATP's stored end-of-day history.
Information and education only, not investment advice.
